data.title: Tesla Cybercab Heads to China, Australia and New Zealand on International Tour
data.description:
Tesla is taking the Cybercab on an international tour, giving the public in China, Australia and New Zealand an opportunity to see its purpose-built robotaxi up close.

For China, the Cybercab will be heading to Beijing and Shanghai, where the vehicle will make its Chinese debut on September 17. Tesla will display the vehicle at its Huamao experience store in Beijing through September 27, while the Shanghai showcase at HKRI Taikoo Hui will run until September 21.

Separately, the tour will all be taking place much further south, with Tesla confirming Cybercab appearances in seven Australian cities before arriving in New Zealand.

Sydney will be the first Australian stop in September, followed by Brisbane, the Gold Coast and Canberra in October. Melbourne and Adelaide are scheduled for November, with Perth rounding out the Australian portion in December. The Cybercab will reach Auckland sometime in 2027.

Tesla has not yet announced exact venues or dates for most of the Australia and New Zealand tour. On the event website, the company says they are “finalizing event details across the tour,” and as events are confirmed, they’ll be added to the website.

Unlike Tesla’s current vehicles, the two-seat Cybercab has no steering wheel, pedals or traditional rearview mirrors. It was designed specifically for autonomous ride-hailing and relies entirely on Tesla’s self-driving technology.

After being revealed at the “We, Robot” event in October 2024, the first production Cybercab rolled off the line at Giga Texas in February 2026. Volume production began in April, followed by the start of public rides in Austin on September 4.

data.title: Waymo Launches Driverless Robotaxi Service in Las Vegas
data.description:
Waymo has officially launched its autonomous ride-hailing service in its 15th U.S. city – Las Vegas.

The Alphabet-owned company began offering paid rides to the public on Monday. Riders are being added on a rolling basis, with Waymo initially deploying a few dozen vehicles before expanding the fleet over time.

The launch also marks the public debut of Waymo’s sixth-generation autonomous driving system in Las Vegas. Rides will be provided using the Ojai, a purpose-built robotaxi based on a vehicle platform from Chinese automaker Zeekr.

“Cruising down Las Vegas Boulevard in a Waymo will make anyone feel like a high roller. Our Ojai vehicle offers a spacious cabin, large screens and a load of customizations that help riders arrive safe and comfortable, throughout our nearly 24-mile service area,” Waymo said in a statement.

The service area will give riders access to parts of Las Vegas Boulevard along with neighbourhoods and major destinations around the city. Waymo has not yet provided full details on the boundaries of the initial operating area or whether highway driving will be available from launch.

Las Vegas is becoming an increasingly competitive testing ground for autonomous ride-hailing. Amazon-owned Zoox launched paid public rides in the city earlier this month. Tesla has also been approved to deploy up to 5,000 Robotaxis in the city.

Waymo, meanwhile, has been accelerating its expansion throughout 2026. The company recently announced plans for Denver, San Diego and Tampa, adding to established operations in markets including California, Arizona, Texas and Florida.

data.title: Tesla expands Semi Charging for Business to Europe as Semi debuts in Germany
data.description:
Tesla is wasting little time preparing the infrastructure needed to support the Semi in Europe. On the same day the European version of the electric truck made its public debut at IAA Transportation in Hannover, Germany, Tesla expanded its new Semi Charging for Business program to five European markets.

According to a post from the Tesla Charging account on X, the program is now available in Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, and the United Kingdom, allowing businesses and fleet operators to purchase Tesla charging equipment for their own properties.

Tesla launched the program in North America earlier this year, offering both its high-powered Megacharger and lower-cost Basecharger.

The expansion to Europe comes as Tesla prepares to begin Semi deliveries in the region in 2027. The European-spec truck made its debut Monday during the press day for IAA Transportation, giving potential customers their first close look at the version specifically designed for the region.

As we reported last week, the European Semi will initially be offered with an estimated range of 550 km (342 miles), based on a total combination weight of 40 tonnes. Tesla estimates energy consumption at 1.0 kWh/km, while charging capability is listed at up to 800 kW. The truck can recover around 60% of its range in 30 minutes, and has a curb weight of less than 9,100 kg (20,062 lbs).

One unique design change made possible due to European regulations is the lack of traditional side mirrors, which have instead been replaced with cameras.

data.title: Tesla Takes First Step Toward Launching in Vietnam
data.description:
Tesla appears to be preparing for another expansion in Southeast Asia, registering a new subsidiary in Vietnam.

According to a newly published business registration filing, Tesla Motors Vietnam Limited Liability Company was officially registered in Ho Chi Minh City on September 11. The company was established with charter capital of 77.667 billion dong, or approximately US$3 million. (via Reuters)

The license gives Tesla a fairly broad scope of operations, including the wholesale and retail sale of vehicles and parts, along with machinery and equipment. It also covers import, export and distribution activities.

David Jon Feinstein, Tesla’s Global Senior Director of Trade & Markets Finance, is listed as chairman of the new company. Isabel Ching Fan, Tesla’s Senior Regional Director for Hong Kong, Macau, the Philippines and Southeast Asia, is named General Director, while Nguyen Manh Hung is listed as her assistant.

While the filing doesn’t guarantee Tesla will begin selling cars in Vietnam in the near future, establishing a local entity is the first step the company takes before entering a new market. Tesla has yet to add Vietnam to its website or announce plans for stores, Service Centres or Superchargers.

If Tesla does move forward, it will be entering one of the fastest-growing EV markets in the world where sales have more than doubled in 2025, with EVs approaching 40% of new vehicle sales.

Tesla would also be taking on a particularly strong local competitor. While VinFast has struggled to gain any sort of market share in North America, the Vietnam-based automaker delivered 175,099 EVs locally last year and was estimated to control nearly the entire EV market.

data.title: Hyundai Delays Atria AI Self-Driving Rollout Until 2029
data.description:
Hyundai is “deliberately delaying ” the rollout of its homegrown autonomous driving software, Atria AI, until 2029 to focus on data collection and machine learning.

The slower rollout timeline will allow the system to reach the internal target of being a true Level 2++ system without the issues that have plagued competitors.

The Atria AI is built on a data flywheel concept where the more data accumulates through road tests, the sharper the AI becomes. Hyundai is using 40 vehicles to collect the data, and engineers are using two systems in parallel to train the AI.

The Hard Example Mining systems will automatically flag driving situations that the model struggles with, while the Special Event Recorder will log data when the car abruptly accelerates, brakes, or the system disengages autonomous braking mode.

In terms of a rollout plan, Kwon Jung-Hyun, lead of the 42dot autonomous driving division, had this to say:

Through 2027, we’ll focus on bringing driving, parking and active-safety features to a high level of polish at the product level. 2028 will be devoted to gathering vast amounts of edge-case data to build a genuinely safe product. And 2029 is when we’ll prepare for safety certification, not just in Korea but in North America and Europe as well.

So, 2029 is the target for Atria, and the company has also confirmed it plans to release a second-half lineup of Hyundai cars equipped with the new self-driving tech but has not confirmed what models are included in this release.

data.title: Tesla FSD owners in Australia can now get cheaper insurance
data.description:
An Australian auto insurance companies is changing how it calculates insurance premiums for Tesla owners. Zurich Australian Insurance Limited has become the country’s first insurer to recognize Full Self-Driving (FSD) as a factor that can lower the cost of coverage through its InsureMyTesla product.

Zurich says the change is based on local and international Tesla data showing vehicles using FSD are involved in roughly seven times fewer major or minor collisions than regular electric vehicles.

Eligible Tesla owners with FSD will now be able to receive more affordable premiums reflecting that lower claimed collision risk. Zurich has not disclosed exactly how large the savings will be.

While this is an Australian first, Zurich isn’t the first insurer globally to take FSD into account. In January, U.S. insurer Lemonade launched its Autonomous Car insurance, which cuts the per-mile insurance rate by 50% for miles driven using FSD. With the owner’s permission, Lemonade connects directly to the vehicle through Tesla’s Fleet API to distinguish between FSD and manually driven miles.

Zurich is taking a slightly different approach, using FSD as a rating factor rather than applying a specific discount based on each mile driven with the system.

“This is a really exciting milestone – both for Tesla owners who are rapidly adopting this FSD (Supervised) technology, and for Zurich as the first insurer in Australia to actively lean into this space. The data shows that drivers using this technology are involved in far fewer accidents, so it’s important they can access insurance that reflects this lower risk,” said Zurich Product Manager David Toma.

The change comes less than a year after Tesla launched FSD in Australia and New Zealand in October 2025. Owners logged one million kilometres on FSD within the first two weeks, while Australian Teslas have now accumulated more than 132 million kilometres using the system.

“We’re pleased to see the insurance industry recognising the safety and value of FSD (Supervised). The data is clear – FSD (Supervised) is making driving significantly safer, and it’s encouraging to see InsureMyTesla by Zurich pioneering this benefit and reflecting the reduced risk for Tesla owners,” said Tesla Australia and New Zealand Country Director Thom Drew.

While Canada has had FSD since 2022, no insurance companies have implemented a similar discount for Canadian Tesla owners who have a FSD license or subscription.

data.title: Tesla Improves Cybertruck Charging Curve With Improved 4680 Cells and Firmware
data.description:
Tesla has quietly made improvements to the Cybertruck’s charging curve, thanks to multiple improvements to its in-house 4680 battery cells and the firmware that controls how the pack charges.

The details come from Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill, who has been sharing some of the many changes Tesla has made to the electric pickup since production began in late 2023. According to Morrill, his team has been able to cut several minutes from the Cybertruck’s 10% to 80% charging time.

“In-house 4680 cells got better, several times actually. And the firmware controls improved as well – both enabled faster Supercharging. Hitting 500kW peak and more importantly shrinking the 10% to 80% charge times by several minutes,” Morrill said.

While hitting a 500kW peak is impressive, we already knew the Cybertruck could achieve that. Morrill highlighted the reduction in overall charging time as more important. Tesla hasn’t said exactly how many minutes have been shaved off a 10% to 80% session, but the gains have come from improvements on both sides of the equation.

According to Morrill, Tesla’s in-house 4680 cells have been improved several times since Cybertruck production began. At the same time, engineers have refined the firmware controlling the battery during fast charging, allowing the truck to sustain a more aggressive charging curve and spend less time plugged in.

The charging improvements are another example of how much the Cybertruck has changed without receiving a traditional refresh. Other recent changes include new composite underbody panels that are lighter and more aerodynamic, along with a redesigned side repeater camera housing that uses airflow to help keep water off the lens.

The latest comments also come shortly after Tesla reached another milestone with its in-house 4680 program. Earlier this month, Tesla built its first Cybertruck using 4680 cells containing lithium refined at its own Gulf Coast Lithium Refinery in Texas.

data.title: 2026 Tesla Model 3 Earns Five-Star NHTSA Safety Rating Across Every Category
data.description:
The 2026 Tesla Model 3 has received the highest possible overall safety rating from the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), earning five stars in every category tested by the agency.

The achievement was announced by the Tesla North America on X, which highlighted that the electric sedan achieved five-star ratings in the frontal crash, side crash and rollover categories, along with a five-star overall score.

NHTSA’s frontal test simulates a head-on collision between two similarly sized vehicles, while its side-impact evaluations include crashes involving another vehicle and a fixed object such as a utility pole. The rollover rating estimates a vehicle’s risk of rolling over during a single-vehicle crash.

The latest result continues the Model 3’s strong history in independent crash testing. Previous versions of the electric sedan have also earned five-star NHTSA ratings, including five stars in each individual category when the original Model 3 was evaluated.

Like Tesla’s other vehicles, the Model 3 benefits from an electric platform that places the battery pack beneath the passenger compartment. This contributes to a low centre of gravity, helping reduce rollover risk. The absence of a conventional engine under the hood also gives engineers more room to design the front structure to absorb energy during a collision.

The Model 3’s result comes less than two weeks after the 2026 Model Y earned the IIHS Top Safety Pick+ designation.

data.title: Tesla Roadster may have been spotted testing cold gas thrusters back in April
data.description:
Over the weekend Tesla finally set a date for the Roadster unveiling – October 1 in Waco, Texas. The decision to hold the event in Waco and not Giga Texas immediately raised one question – why? The answer could be sitting outside Waco at SpaceX’s rocket development and testing facility in McGregor, where some interesting footage captured earlier this year has now resurfaced.

The video was recorded by NASASpaceflight on April 15, the same month Tesla was at one point expected to reveal the Roadster. It shows a large covered structure at the McGregor facility, with an unidentified object being raised vertically inside. On its own, however, there is nothing in the footage that directly links the object to Tesla or the Roadster.

But with previous reports pointing specifically to McGregor as the location where Tesla planned to test and demonstrate the Roadster’s SpaceX-developed thrusters, the footage is getting a closer look ahead of the October 1 event.

A Roadster silhouette was overlayed on the object, and it looks remarkably like the vehicle’s recently revealed wordmark. We can also see cold gas thrusters being tested by an object on the ground, with the gas emerging through the tent structure.

However, there is currently no evidence confirming the object in the video is a Roadster, or even that the footage shows testing related to the vehicle. TheSpaceEngineer later clarified that the object being lifted into the air wasn’t flying under its own power.

“This is being lifted by a gantry, not it flying,” he explained, adding that the covered structure contains a large lifting system.

Why McGregor Is Getting Attention

The speculation becomes more interesting when combined with what has emerged about Tesla’s October 1 event. Invitations sent to Roadster reservation holders confirm the event will take place in Waco, Texas. SpaceX’s McGregor facility is located roughly 35 minutes outside the city, making it an obvious candidate for where Tesla could demonstrate the vehicle’s more extreme capabilities.

That also lines up with an August report from The Information, which said Tesla was planning to demonstrate a Roadster equipped with SpaceX-developed cold-gas thrusters at McGregor. The vehicle would reportedly lift off the ground while being remotely operated, with spectators positioned hundreds of yards away because of the noise. Tesla has not confirmed McGregor as the venue.

The company’s latest teaser is only adding fuel to the fire. Tesla announced the October 1 event with the words “Go for launch” alongside an image showing four bright plumes, which we all naturally assumed were SpaceX cold gas thrusters. Also hidden within the image were the words “Where we’re going…”, which is a nod to the iconic ‘Back To The Future’ movie trilogy.

Musk has been talking about using SpaceX thrusters on the Roadster since 2019, when he said the system would use ultra-high-pressure air stored in a composite overwrapped pressure vessel in place of the rear seats.

So while the April footage doesn’t prove Tesla was secretly testing the Roadster at McGregor, the location, timing, and Tesla’s choice of Waco for the October 1 unveiling make the old video considerably more interesting than it was five months ago.

data.title: Tesla’s Grok will soon be able to send text messages
data.description:
Last month we told about over 100 commands that the latest version of Grok can handle inside your Tesla. One capability missing from the list is being able to send text messages, but according to the latest version of the owner’s manual, that is changing soon.

The unreleased feature appears in the Model 3/Y owner’s manual, where it lists a series of capabilities that Grok can handle when the ‘Assistant’ personality is selected. With the latest update to the manual, spotted by Not A Tesla App, drivers will be able to ask Grok to send a message to one of their contacts without having to reach for their phone.

Tesla’s existing voice-to-text system has frequently been criticized for being slow to respond, occasionally glitching, and missing or incorrectly transcribing words. Bringing text messaging into Grok could make the experience more reliable and conversational.

Although the feature is already documented in the manual, it has not yet been activated in Tesla vehicles. The company has also not provided a timeline for its release, but its inclusion in the owner’s manual specific for the 2026.26 software vresion suggests it could be turned on soon through a server-side switch.

What Grok Can Already Do

Grok can already make phone calls, search for destinations, modify navigation routes, and find media using conversational voice commands. Tesla has also been gradually connecting the xAI chatbot to more of the vehicle itself.

As part of the 2026 Summer Update that rolled out last month, the automaker added support for controlling features such as cabin temperature, seat heating and ventilation, steering-wheel heating and the glovebox. Grok can also locate settings within the Controls menu and answer vehicle-related questions using information from the owner’s manual.

Tesla originally introduced Grok in software update 2025.26, initially limiting it to vehicles in the United States. It later expanded to Canada with the 2025.38 software update.

The integration is expected to go even further and incorporate Full Self-Driving (FSD). Elon Musk has previously said you will be able to use conversational voice commands through Grok to tell the vehicle to avoid a particular intersection, take a different entrance, stop at a preferred pickup location, or make other route adjustments, and more.
